conviction_note: Two-thirds of the quarter is already public in the July and August 8-Ks. The only real unknown is September's combined ratio. September looks benign on catastrophes, NPW growth is re-accelerating and the headline comparisons are easy (Q3 2025 CR 89.5 and EPS $4.45 carried a $950M Florida credit). Against that, the ex-cat margin trend has worsened for three straight months, this name sold its Q2 EPS beat by -9.4%, the bar is disputed, puts are bid and the stock is up 5.5% in 5 days. Findings sum to +0.30; the scaled number is p_up 52 x abs 3.8 = +0.15, near zero because the sign is close to a coin flip.
bar: Disputed, so every finding is capped small. Q3 2026 EPS consensus is $3.65 from 15 analysts at TickerLeague (https://tickerleague.com/companies/PGR/estimates, search snippet; the page returned 404 on fetch), $3.98 at Benzinga on 2026-08-31 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PGR/earnings-forecasts, snippet; fetch returned 503) and $3.17-3.67 at TipRanks. July plus August GAAP EPS is already $1.65 + $1.63 = $3.28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000322/pgr202608ex99earningsrelea.htm). The bar the stock actually trades on is the September combined ratio against the monthly trend. Comparables: June 90.0, July 86.8, August 89.3, and September 2025 at 100.4 reported, about 86.5 excluding the Florida credit.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 1.0-1.4% of float with about 2.7 days to cover (Equibles about 2026-08-20, https://equibles.com/stocks/pgr/short-interest; Benzinga about 2026-09-08), so the short is not crowded. 25-delta skew is +4.54 vol points: puts are bid and the market leans downside. Put/call OI is 0.81. Run-up is +5.48% over 5 days and +1.07% over 20 days, with the stock 6.96% below its 52-week high.

findings.finding: September 2026 was a quiet US catastrophe month. El Nino suppressed the Atlantic season, the only US landfall was Tropical Storm Edouard near the Louisiana/Texas line around 1 September, and Swiss Re called the season relatively quiet in mid-September. That points to a low September cat load, unlike August, when a derecho and Hawaii flooding hit (Allstate August cats $748M across 21 events).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The monthly CR is the line PGR trades on. The June CR of 90.0 plus the NPW miss drove -9.43% on 2026-07-15. September 2025's cat ratio was also low (0.9%), so the year-over-year cat comparison is neutral.
findings.why_not_priced: Weather is public, so this is mostly priced. If the market had fully priced a clean September, skew would not be bid at +4.5 vol points into the print. What remains is the transmission to PGR's own ratio, which is not public until the release.
findings.independence: Swiss Re press release of 2026-09-16 says the 2026 Atlantic season has been relatively quiet (https://www.swissre.com/press-release/100-years-after-the-Great-Miami-Hurricane-Florida-hurricane-could-cause-USD-300-billion-or-more-in-insured-losses-finds-Swiss-Re-Institute/eac93803-92d3-4528-82fa-94833ba4146b). This is an industry proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: The headline arithmetic is easy. July plus August GAAP EPS is already $3.28 from the 8-Ks, so the aggregator Q3 consensus of $3.65-3.98 implies September EPS of only $0.37-0.70, below every 2026 month (the lowest was June at $1.34). Q3 2025 (EPS $4.45, CR 89.5) and September 2025 (CR 100.4) both carried the $950M Florida credit. Absent a new one-off, the release headlines a Q3 EPS beat and a year-over-year CR improvement. Florida's statute 627.066(12) books the 2025 refund as a 2025 policyholder dividend, which offsets 2025 in the next three-year test, so a repeat accrual is not implied.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats do not pay on this name. Q2 2026 operating EPS beat ($4.86 against $4.59) and the stock fell 9.43% on the CR and NPW. Q3 2025's Florida charge produced -5.78%.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregator consensus looks stale against the monthly 8-Ks. Holders model the months, though, so this mainly affects headline and algorithmic optics, and the skew does not show a market expecting a beat. The low consensus could also mean some analysts model a repeat September Florida accrual, which would turn this negative.
findings.independence: The September 2025 / Q3 2025 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/80661/000008066125000126/pgr20250930ex99earningsrel.htm) gives the comparison base. The Florida statute text (https://m.flsenate.gov/Statutes/627.066) shows refunds are treated as dividends of the year incurred. Both are separate documents but the same arithmetic thesis.

findings.finding: Underlying margin has worsened three months running and largely outside cats. The August CR was 89.3 against 83.1 (+6.2 points) with a cat ratio of only 1.9%. July was +1.5 points and June +3.4. The September 2025 comparable excluding the Florida credit is about 86.5, so September 2026 likely shows another underlying year-over-year deterioration of about 2-3 points.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin deterioration caused -9.43% on 2026-07-15. In August, Insurance Business reported it as the weakest CR of 2026 with no visible reversal.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The trend is in three public 8-Ks, the stock is down sharply YTD and the skew is bid. The only unpriced part is whether September steepens or flattens the trend.
findings.independence: Both the August 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000322/pgr202608ex99earningsrelea.htm) and the June 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000262/pgr202606ex99earningsrelea.htm) show the CR trend. These are company documents, and the same source family as the growth finding.

findings.finding: Premium growth is re-accelerating after the Q2 miss that drove July's sell-off. NPW grew +3% in June, +5% in July and +6% in August. PIF is steady at +7% (40.49M), with direct auto at +9% and agency auto at +7%. The September 2025 NPW comparison is +8% on $7,128M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 NPW of +5%, below expectations, was half the reason for -9.43% on 2026-07-15. The July release, with NPW +5%, was met with a reported rise of about 4% intraday.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, since the 8-Ks are public. If the re-acceleration were fully credited, the stock would not still sit near the July post-print level with puts bid.
findings.independence: The June 8-K (NPW +3%, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000262/pgr202606ex99earningsrelea.htm) and the July 8-K (NPW +5%, https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3927716/progressive-reports-july-2026-results). These are company documents from the same family.

baseline_tension: The positive lean (benign September cats, easy headline comparisons, growth re-accelerating) cuts against the +4.5-point put skew and the +5.5% 5-day run-up. The negative margin finding agrees with the skew and is mostly priced. That tension is why p_up sits at 52 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar): the EPS-headline finding was cut from +0.6 to +0.3 because the consensus has three disagreeing sources ($3.17-3.98) and two could not be fetched.
Rule 1 (beats sold): the same finding was cut further, from +0.3 to +0.2, because Q2's EPS beat produced -9.4%. p_up moved from 53 to 52.
Rule 5 / 'what has worked' (weather is a proxy): the cat finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest was checked (about 1.4%, not crowded). The negative margin finding agrees with the skew and is mostly priced, so it was cut from -0.5 to -0.4.
The NPW re-acceleration finding (company 8-Ks) was left unchanged at +0.3.
